class: A list presented as the owner's fresh jobs was built from a fixed, narrow source and said nothing about when a job was posted, so the owner could not see the jobs they applied for or tell new from old
symptom: The agent could not fetch recent jobs matching the profile. The owner saw nothing from Workday, ADP, iCIMS or the other systems they apply through; the last scan was days old; and jobs already applied to or rejected were still on the page.
site: job_discovery.py and the Suggested jobs section of web_ui.py, 2 November 2026
root_cause: The scan could read only Greenhouse and Lever job lists, and only for twelve tech companies in a fixed file, while the owner's applications went mostly through Workday, Ashby, iCIMS and others that were never read. No job carried a posting date, so nothing could be filtered by how recently it was posted. Jobs the owner had skipped, been disqualified from, or had in progress were not recognised as already dealt with, because only sent applications counted and they were marked rather than left out. Even for jobs it could read, a wanted title in a place other than Remote, Fairfax or Arlington scored 50, under the 60 cut-off, though the owner's profile says open to relocation: of 614 jobs posted in the last week on the owners' employers' lists, 600 were dropped by that score.
why_tests_missed: Discovery tests fed rows that were already in the database and checked ordering, expiry and scoring; none asked which systems a scan could read, whether the employers the owner actually applies through were among them, whether a job carried a date, or what a time window would show.
fix: New readers (discovery_sources.py) for Workday, Ashby and iCIMS beside Greenhouse and Lever, each returning when the job was posted as exactly as the system says (an exact time, or a day held as the earliest it could be, so a job is only called recent when it certainly is). The employers to scan are taken from the applications already made as well as the owner's list. Each job's posting date is stored; the page offers the last hour, 24 hours, 3 days and week, newest first, and a job with no known date is never in a window. Any job with a record in the owner's history, whatever its status, is left out, as is anything dismissed. ADP is left out until it gives a link that opens a single job. A place other than the owner's, in the owner's own country, earns half the credit of their own place (15 against 30) when the profile says open to relocation, so a wanted title anywhere in the country counts; a loose match (a tech word alone) and another country still do not. The project ships a tested list of multinational employers with offices in India (reference/employers.json: no consultancies, IT-services firms or government contractors) that the scan reads with the owner's list and the history; a title that only narrows another is not searched separately. 'Find new jobs' starts the scan in the background and returns at once (a scan of about a hundred employers took seven minutes); the page says it is checking, a second press starts no second scan.
prevention: A list sold as fresh says when each item was posted, comes from the places the owner actually uses (taken from their history, not a fixed file), and filters on a date it can prove. Anything the owner has already dealt with, in any way, is not offered again. A preference the owner has said they will bend (place, when open to relocation) is a bonus in the score, never a gate; test it with the owner's own stated flexibility.
